observations: Photo 0: A hand holds a black DSLR camera body with a lens attached and the lens cap on, photographed indoors against a wall with a light switch visible.
"Nikon" branding is legible on the camera's pentaprism area.
A watermark reading "STARSHOOT IMAGE" overlays the photo.
The lens front element is covered by a cap, so glass condition cannot be seen.
No screen, LCD display, serial number plate, or shutter-count readout is visible in this photo.
No battery, charger, strap, box, or accessories are shown.
Only one angle/one photo is provided for the entire listing.

read_from: photo 0 body badge shows 'Nikon' brand only

claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows 'Nikon' branding but the specific model number D810 is not legibly readable in the image.
Lens barrel markings are not legible in photo 0; lens cap is on, obscuring front element and any printed specs.
No screenshot of camera menu or third-party shutter-count-reading software is shown; seller's verbal claim of testing it himself is not visual proof.

claims.claim: No fungus or scratch on the lens
claims.evidence: Lens cap is on in photo 0; front and rear elements are not visible.
No battery or charger is shown in photo 0.
No internal, serial-number, or service-sticker evidence is shown.

claims.claim: "I tested it myself yesterday, everything I said is true"
claims.evidence: This is a verbal assurance with no accompanying photo or video; seller's words are not proof of condition or specs.

risks.risk: Model number could be a cheaper/older Nikon body (e.g. D800 vs D810) misstated by seller.
risks.proof: Clear close-up photo of the model badge/nameplate on the body, and the serial number sticker on the base.
risks.if_unproven: priced as the lowest-value plausible full-frame Nikon DSLR body in this generation

risks.risk: Lens could be a lower-spec or third-party 24-70mm (e.g. f/4 or non-Nikon) rather than the premium f/2.8 Nikkor.
risks.proof: Photo of lens barrel with cap off showing printed model/aperture, and a shot of the mount.
risks.if_unproven: priced as the lowest-value generic 24-70mm lens option

risks.risk: Actual shutter count may be far higher than claimed, affecting mechanical wear and resale value.
risks.proof: Screenshot from shutter-count app (e.g. Nikon menu, or third-party EXIF/shutter count tool) showing current count.
risks.if_unproven: priced as high shutter count / heavily used body

risks.risk: Lens glass may have fungus, haze, or scratches hidden by the cap.
risks.proof: Photo of front and rear lens elements with cap removed, held up to light.
risks.if_unproven: priced as lens with optical defects

risks.risk: Camera may not power on or autofocus/shutter may be faulty.
risks.proof: Short video showing power-on, live view, autofocus engaging, and a test shutter fire.

risks.risk: Missing accessories (battery, charger, box) despite being claimed.
risks.proof: Photo showing battery, charger, and any included box/strap together with the camera.
risks.if_unproven: priced as body+lens only, no accessories

risks.risk: Body could have hidden physical damage (dents, drop marks, loose mount) not visible from this single angle.
risks.proof: Additional photos from top, back (LCD/screen), bottom (tripod mount/serial), and lens mount area.
risks.if_unproven: priced as cosmetic condition unknown, assume moderate wear

proof_requests: Clear photo of the camera's model nameplate/badge and serial number sticker.
Photo of the lens barrel (cap off) showing printed model, focal length, and aperture markings.
Screenshot of shutter count from camera menu or shutter-count software.
Photos of front and rear lens elements with cap removed, under good light.
Short video of camera powering on, autofocusing, and firing the shutter.
Photos of included battery, charger, and any box/accessories.
Additional body photos: top view, rear LCD screen, and base/tripod mount.
response.reason: The seller's reassurance is text only and does not change what the photo shows; no model nameplate, serial number, lens markings, shutter-count screenshot, or functional video has been provided, so a worst-case price still cannot be set.
